findings.quote: The shortcut applies to this pair of units only. To go from $\text{m/s}$ to $\text{km/h}$, multiply by $3.6$.
findings.problem: Round-2 L22a is fixed in Core Concept, but this Speed Tricks paragraph on chained conversions has four sentences, over the one-to-three-sentence limit.

The single display line in Example #5 holds three stacked fractions, two equals signs and two more results. At display size it is wider than a phone screen and will scroll or shrink. It could be split across two display lines.
findings.source: Checklist L21; LSG Examples section (keep each display equation narrow enough for a phone screen)

findings.quote: A sample has a mass of $4.5\ \text{mg}$. Express it in kilograms.
findings.problem: First use of the exam instruction word "express", which the style guide names as needing a one-line meaning on first use. The lesson never says that "express" here means convert and give the value in that unit.
findings.source: Checklist L03; LSG Voice (exam instruction words such as express)
